snapshot_field_meaning: decode_snapshot -- the date the EPC decode and the series-to-tonnage mapping behind this file were taken. It is NOT the billing window; read `billing_through` for that.

clock_definition.FY: ISZE year, April to March, labelled by the closing year (FY2026 = April 2025 to March 2026)

tie_out.components_note: single_band + shared_across_bands + series_unresolved + no_series_found = the in-family total. The evolution file files the last two together as one `series_unresolved` membership, so its unresolved euro equals the band file's series_unresolved plus no_series_found.

rules: A series is matched as a whole token, never as a substring. Wildcard tokens (N*, N*R) are recorded and never converted into a band.
A part number that fits more than one band is pooled as shared_across_bands and is never apportioned across the bands it fits.

A part number that names both a series the sources resolve and one they do not is pooled, never called exclusive: the unreadable code may sit at any rung, so the readable ones cannot narrow the part to a single band. `widened` tests that directly, off the codes each route handed back with no band, and `believed` is then the widest honest band set for the row. Until 2026-09-24 the test read the unknown half off a list already filtered to the codes that DO resolve, so it was empty and the branch never ran; six part numbers were being reported as exclusive to one band on the strength of the codes we can read, and in silence about the ones we cannot.

band_count is the number of bands listed in tonnage_band, and band_status says the same thing: single_band means exactly one, shared_across_bands means two or more, series_unresolved and no_series_found mean none. The two columns are asserted against each other before this file is written, so a row that counts a band it does not carry - the shape that sat in this file for three revisions on part number 5876100771 - stops the build instead of being written. One legal shape lists a single band beside a shared status: a row that names an unplaced code, where the band it can read is written down but a second band cannot be named. That shape is recognised only when series_unresolved is non-empty, so a row that merely miscounts its own bands still fails. That one part number is exempt by name while an EPC fitment answer is outstanding; it is printed on every build and written unchanged, and it is an exception to be closed, not a precedent.
A series neither authorised source names leaves the band blank, with the reason written in band_reason.

A part number outside the N-series family (EPC 'TRUCKS N' but also a heavy or light vehicle part) is not put in a band: it belongs to the pooled family row of the parent page, and banding it here would double-count it.

The three bands plus the pool plus the unresolved group sum to the tagged N-series billing, asserted at build time. 'The unresolved group' means both band_status buckets with no band - series_unresolved (a series is named but none resolves) and no_series_found (no series named at all); the evolution file carries the two as one `series_unresolved` membership. Without no_series_found the sum falls short.
